admin.secret_scanning.desc: Scans every push and the wiki of every repository for credentials and raises an alert per secret. The secret itself is never stored.
admin.secret_scanning.app_ini: Starting values come from %s; a value saved here wins.
admin.secret_scanning.read_only: You can read this page; only a site administrator can change it.
admin.secret_scanning.enable: Enable secret scanning on this instance
admin.secret_scanning.enable_help: Off: nothing is scanned anywhere and no alert is updated. Existing alerts are kept but hidden.
admin.secret_scanning.generic_help: Also finds long random-looking strings that no known token format matches. It is noisy: expect false positives such as hashes, checksums and test data. It applies to new scans only.
admin.secret_scanning.scan_text: Scan issues, pull requests and comments
admin.secret_scanning.scan_text_help: Also looks for secrets in the titles, bodies and comments of issues and pull requests (new and edited text, and the text that is there already). Alerts show the issue or comment number, never the text. Off: that text is not scanned; existing alerts are kept.
admin.secret_scanning.file_default_on: %s turns it on; the value saved here wins.
admin.secret_scanning.file_default_off: %s leaves it off; the value saved here wins.

admin.secret_scanning.site_off_title: Stop secret scanning on all repositories?
admin.secret_scanning.site_off_confirm: No push will be scanned and no alert updated until it is turned back on. Existing alerts are kept but hidden. Recorded in the audit log.
admin.secret_scanning.generic_title: Turn on the generic high-entropy rule?
admin.secret_scanning.generic_confirm: It applies to new scans only; existing repositories are not scanned again. Expect many false positives (hashes, checksums, test data), and its alerts count toward each repository's limit. Recorded in the audit log.
admin.secret_scanning.limits_at_limit: A scan that hits a limit stops and the repository shows "Scan incomplete: limit reached".
admin.secret_scanning.limits_floors: Lowest values: %s per scan slice, %s for the largest file, %s and %s read per slice, %s per repository. Locations per alert: at least %s.
admin.secret_scanning.limits_help: They protect the server. Under each field is its default from app.ini.
admin.secret_scanning.limit.max_text_byt: Most text scanned per issue or comment
admin.secret_scanning.error.nothing_save: Nothing was saved. %s must be at least %s and at most %s.
admin.secret_scanning.error.invalid: Nothing was saved. %s must be a number.

secret_pattern.title: Custom patterns
secret_pattern.intro_reader: Patterns the organization and the site scan for, on top of the built-in rules. Alerts are named after the pattern.
secret_pattern.intro_site_reader: Patterns the site scans every repository for, on top of the built-in rules. Alerts are named after the pattern.
secret_pattern.intro: Extra patterns that repositories are scanned for, on top of the built-in rules. A pattern needs 1 to 5 keywords and is checked before it is saved. Matches raise alerts named after the pattern. Only the name can be changed later; a site pattern also applies to every organization.
secret_pattern.name: Name
secret_pattern.manage: Manage the patterns in the organization settings
secret_pattern.count: %d of %d patterns are on, including the site's. If the site adds patterns later and the total passes %[2]d, the newest ones are skipped.
secret_pattern.count_site: %d of %d site patterns are on. Site patterns count toward every organization's limit of %[2]d.
secret_pattern.pattern_help: RE2 syntax, matched against each file's text. It can't be edited after saving.
secret_pattern.keywords_help: A keyword is text every match contains, such as the token's prefix (for example acme_). Files are searched only where a keyword appears.
secret_pattern.sample_help: An example secret the pattern must find. It is checked and thrown away: never stored, logged or shown back.
secret_pattern.test_failed: The test could not be run
secret_pattern.test_rate_limited: Too many tests, try again in a minute.
secret_pattern.test_ok.title: Match found
secret_pattern.test_ok.text: The pattern found a secret of %d characters (it starts %s) and every keyword is in the match. Nothing was stored.
secret_pattern.audit_note: Adding, renaming, enabling, disabling and deleting a pattern is recorded in the audit log.
secret_pattern.added: The pattern %s was added. Pushes from now on are scanned for it; history is not scanned again.
secret_pattern.rename_help: Only the name changes: the pattern and its keywords are fixed, so alerts keep their meaning.

secret_pattern.disable_text.one: Repositories stop being scanned for it from the next push. Its %s open alert stays open. You can enable it again.
secret_pattern.disable_text.other: Repositories stop being scanned for it from the next push. Its %s open alerts stay open. You can enable it again.

secret_pattern.disable_text_none: Repositories stop being scanned for it from the next push. It has no open alerts. You can enable it again.

secret_pattern.delete_text.one: Repositories are no longer scanned for it. Its %s open alert stays, labelled "deleted pattern". The pattern can't be restored.
secret_pattern.delete_text.other: Repositories are no longer scanned for it. Its %s open alerts stay, labelled "deleted pattern". The pattern can't be restored.

secret_pattern.delete_text_none: Repositories are no longer scanned for it. It has no open alerts. The pattern can't be restored.
secret_pattern.delete_confirm_failed: The name you typed is not the pattern's name, so nothing was deleted.
secret_pattern.locked_archived: This organization is archived: patterns can't be added or changed.
secret_pattern.locked_maintenance: The instance is in read-only maintenance mode: patterns can't be added or changed.
secret_pattern.site_off: Secret scanning is off on this instance, so patterns have no effect yet. They can be prepared here.
secret_pattern.err_title.name: Invalid name
secret_pattern.err_text.name: A name has 1 to 64 characters, with no control characters and no invisible or text-direction characters.
secret_pattern.err_text.name_taken: Another pattern of this owner has that name.
secret_pattern.err_text.too_long: A pattern has at most 1024 bytes.
secret_pattern.err_text.invalid: The pattern is not a valid RE2 regular expression. Check its brackets and escapes.
secret_pattern.err_text.invalid_repeat: A repeat (*, +, ? or {n}) has nothing before it, or is repeated itself, near "%s".
secret_pattern.err_text.invalid_repeat_s: A repeat count is above 1000 or its range is backwards: "%s".
secret_pattern.err_text.invalid_perl: Lookaheads, lookbehinds and backreferences aren't supported by RE2.
secret_pattern.err_text.invalid_near: Check the brackets and escapes near "%s".
secret_pattern.err_text.complex: It would take too long to run on large files. Make it shorter or more specific: no open-ended repeats, no repeat inside a repeat.
secret_pattern.err_text.empty: The pattern matches the empty string. Make it require some text.
secret_pattern.err_text.common: The pattern matched a sample of ordinary source code. Make it more specific.
secret_pattern.err_text.keyword_common: A keyword appears in ordinary text, so the pattern would be looked for almost everywhere. Use a keyword that is specific to the secret, such as its prefix.
secret_pattern.err_text.holds_secret: The name, the pattern or a keyword contains text in a known token format. They are shown to other people and written to the audit log, so they can't hold a real token: put only the token's shape in the pattern.
secret_pattern.err_text.keywords: A pattern needs 1 to 5 keywords of 3 to 64 characters, and every one must appear in the match of the test string.
secret_pattern.err_title.keywords_match: A keyword must appear in the match
secret_pattern.err_text.keywords_match: Every keyword must be in the text the pattern matches in the test string.
secret_pattern.err_text.keywords_match_f: The pattern matched a string that starts %s, and not every keyword is in it.
secret_pattern.err_text.holds_secret_nam: The name contains text in a known token format (%s). Names are shown to other people and written to the audit log, so they can't hold a real token.
secret_pattern.err_text.holds_secret_pat: The pattern contains text in a known token format (%s). Patterns are written to the audit log, so they can't hold a real token: put only the token's shape in the pattern.
secret_pattern.err_text.holds_secret_key: A keyword contains text in a known token format (%s). Keywords are shown to other people, so they can't hold a real token: use a fixed prefix or label.
secret_pattern.err_text.no_match: The pattern didn't match the test string.
secret_pattern.err_text.short: The secret found in the test string must have at least 8 characters.
secret_pattern.err_text.short_found: The pattern found a string that starts %s and has %d characters; a secret needs at least 8.
secret_pattern.err_text.sample_long: The test string has at most 4096 bytes.
secret_pattern.err_text.live_limit: At most %d patterns, on or off, can be kept. Delete one first.
secret_pattern.err_text.limit: At most %d patterns can be on at once, the site's included. Turn one off or delete it first.
admin.audit.action.org.secret_alerts.exp: Exported the secret alerts of organization %s
admin.audit.action.admin.secret_alerts.e: Exported the secret alerts of every owner
repo.secrets.redact.title: Redact the secret
repo.secrets.redact.replace: Every copy of the secret still in this text is replaced with %s. The rest of the text stays as it is.
repo.secrets.redact.history: Its earlier versions are deleted from the edit history. If the secret is already gone from the text, only the versions that hold it.
repo.secrets.redact.undo: This can't be undone. The edit is shown as yours, and nobody is notified.
repo.secrets.redact.revoke: The credential still works until you revoke it. Notification mails, webhook deliveries and other copies already sent keep the secret.
repo.secrets.redact.done: The secret was replaced with %s and its earlier versions were deleted from the edit history. Revoke it, then close the alert.
repo.secrets.redact.gone: Nothing left to remove: the secret is no longer in this text or its edit history.
repo.secrets.redact.changed: Someone edited the text at the same moment. Nothing was removed: try again.
repo.secrets.redact.manual: This text can't be redacted automatically. Edit it by hand, then delete its old versions from the "edited" menu.
repo.secrets.redact.done_title: The secret was replaced with %s in the title and in the title changes of the timeline. Revoke it, then close the alert.
repo.secrets.redact.history_only: The secret was already gone from the text. Its earlier versions were deleted from the edit history.
repo.secrets.redact.history_only_title: The secret was already gone from the title. It was removed from the title changes of the timeline.
repo.secrets.redact.pattern: The pattern that found this secret was deleted or turned off, so it can't be found again. Edit the text by hand, then delete its old versions from the "edited" menu.
repo.secrets.redact.history_title: The secret is also removed from the title changes in the timeline (a title has no edit history).
repo.secrets.redact.marked_removed: The secret was already gone from this text and nothing else here held it. Its place is now marked removed.
repo.secrets.activity.redacted_history: cleaned up an issue or pull request text the secret was already gone from
repo.secrets.activity.redacted: removed the secret from an issue or pull request text
admin.audit.action.repo.secret_alert.tex: Removed the secret of the alert for %s from the text of an issue or pull request
